data.title: Atlassian Rovo Exfiltrates Data, Bypassing Controls
data.author: hackerBanana
data.article_summary:
Atlassian Rovo AI存在严重数据泄露漏洞。攻击者可通过间接提示注入(如在上传文件中隐藏恶意指令)窃取Jira工单和Confluence文档等敏感数据。攻击原理是操纵Rovo的URL检索工具,将数据附加到攻击者URL上,当Rovo访问该URL时,攻击者服务器日志即可记录泄露的数据。

该攻击无需人工审批即可执行,且即使组织禁用了Rovo的网页搜索功能也无法防御,因为该设置未能移除打开搜索结果的工具。PromptArmor于2026年5月23日向Atlassian披露此漏洞,但两个多月后Atlassian未做进一步响应,漏洞至今未修复。研究人员公开发布以警示用户风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Atlassian Rovo的安全性、隐私问题和产品设计

不同观点：

• **隐私和数据使用担忧**：多位用户指出Atlassian默认开启数据用于AI训练（8月17日生效），且Rovo会下载所有可访问文档到AWS服务器进行"分析"，涉及Google Docs和Sharepoint等外部资源

• **安全漏洞的严重性存在分歧**：技术派认为URL检索工具缺乏保护、存在prompt注入风险，可被操纵泄露敏感数据；而怀疑派认为这些攻击需要受害者主动输入恶意提示，实际利用条件苛刻

• **产品体验普遍差评**：用户抱怨Rovo强制注入到每个JIRA和Confluence页面，导致加载变慢、界面臃肿，且极难禁用（需昂贵套餐才能关闭），"Rovo"这个名字本身也被批评

• **AI安全的通用问题**：有评论指出这是所有现代AI代理系统的共同弱点——私有数据访问+不可信内容+外部通信能力的"致命三要素"

补充讨论：技术解决方案方面，有人建议采用Anthropic的URL白名单模式，只允许访问用户输入或可信工具返回的URL；也有人质疑文章质量和攻击细节的模糊性。

49185983.article_content:
Atlassian Rovo AI exfiltrates data, bypassing controls: attacker logs contain Jira tickets and Confluence docs.
Context
Atlassian’s Rovo AI is a multi-purpose agent that operates across Atlassian’s product suite (Jira, Confluence, etc.).
Vulnerabilities have been identified that enable data exfiltration across an Atlassian tenant (Jira tickets, Confluence docs, etc.) via indirect prompt injection. This attack executes without requiring any human-in-the-loop approval, and succeeds by exploiting Rovo's URL retrieval tool.
This attack succeeds even if an organization has disabled web search for Rovo. This is because the web search setting fails to remove the tool for opening the search results.
PromptArmor disclosed the vulnerabilities covered in this article to Atlassian on May 23rd. Atlassian assigned a case number and expressed thanks, but after multiple follow-ups by PromptArmor over more than two months, Atlassian has made no further communication, and Rovo remains vulnerable. As such, we are publishing to inform users of the risks.
The Attack Chain
1.
The victim prepares a query asking Rovo to organize Jira tickets
The victim enters a query into Rovo
2.
The victim uploads a file to Rovo that contains a hidden prompt injection
For general use cases, this is quite common: a user finds a file online and uploads it to Rovo. This attack is not dependent on the injection source - other injection sources include, but are not limited to: external data in Atlassian (e.g., support tickets), web data (if search is enabled), third-party ‘connectors’, etc.
The 'Backlog Guide' document uploaded by the user contains a concealed prompt injection.
3.
The victim asks Rovo to organize their Jira tickets
Rovo processes the request and begins searching Jira and Confluence.
4.
The injection manipulates Rovo to submit Jira tickets and Confluence documents to the attacker’s website
Rovo's URL retrieval tool is insecure:
there are no protections against opening a URL that has been dynamically created by the agent
. Here, Rovo is manipulated to append sensitive data to an attacker's URL. When Rovo calls the insecure tool to open the URL, the attacker's site logs the request, including the appended sensitive data.
Rovo is manipulated by the injection to submit Jira and Confluence data to the attacker's URL.
Note: This attack succeeds even if an organization has disabled web search for Rovo. This is because the web search setting fails to remove the tool for opening the search results.
The organization-wide 'Enable web search' setting for Rovo is toggled off.
If the user returns to the chat later, they see the agent's suggested ticket updates, but no evidence of the attack.
If the user later reopens the chat, all evidence is gone and output appears normal.
5.
The attacker views the victim’s tickets and document contents in their website logs
The prompt injection can exfiltrate any data the agent can access in Atlassian, including any data the agent can access via ‘connectors’.
The attacker's server logs contain the exfiltrated Jira tickets and Confluence documents.
Extra: A second exfiltration mechanism
Atlassian Rovo also renders Markdown images from AI outputs. Insecure Markdown image rendering is a well-known vector for data exfiltration via indirect prompt injection.
To see what a full attack chain looks like for insecure Markdown image rendering, here are some examples from our other research:
■
Codex Exfiltrates Connector Data
■
OpenAI API Logs Data Exfiltration
■
Superhuman AI Exfiltrates Emails
■
Hugging Face Chat Exfiltrates Data
■
Data Exfiltration from Writer.com via Indirect Prompt Injection
Responsible Disclosure
PromptArmor disclosed the vulnerabilities covered in this article to Atlassian on May 23rd. Atlassian assigned a case number and expressed thanks, but after multiple follow-ups by PromptArmor over more than two months, Atlassian has made no further communication, and Rovo remains vulnerable as of the release of this article.

data.title: Nvidia’s Vera Whitepaper Has a Thread Loose
data.author: pella
data.article_summary:
NVIDIA发布了首款服务器CPU Vera的白皮书，搭载88核Olympus处理器（10宽度Arm v9.2架构），配备价值预测、图预取器、2MB私有L2缓存、164MB共享缓存和1.2TB/s内存带宽。

文章批评白皮书过度营销，试图将技术选择包装成针对x86的"道德叙事"。作者指出Olympus的核心技术（神经分支预测、图预取等）并非全新，Intel和AMD早已有类似实现。

尽管如此，独立测试显示Vera性能强劲：比AMD EPYC 9575F快10%，比Intel Xeon 6980P快1.55倍，是目前公开测试中最强的Arm服务器CPU。

NVIDIA’s Vera Whitepaper Has a Thread Loose
George Cozma
and
Chester Lam
Aug 05, 2026
36
3
1
Share
Hello you fine Internet folks,
NVIDIA has
published a 45-page whitepaper explaining Vera
, its first server CPU built around the company’s own Olympus core. On paper, Vera is a fascinating chip with an 88-core monolithic compute die, Olympus being a 10-wide Arm v9.2 core that has value prediction, a graph prefetcher, 2 MB of private L2 per core, 164 MB of shared last-level cache, and eight LPDDR5X memory interfaces promising 1.2 TB/s.
Unfortunately, NVIDIA also spends a good part of the paper trying to turn those interesting design choices into a morality play about x86. Traditional simultaneous multithreading is drawn as time-slicing, a configurable NUMA topology is presented as an unavoidable 32-node maze, four SPEC components become “agentic benchmarks,” undefined performance-counter ratios are promoted as causal proof, and an unlabeled pictogram becomes a 1.8x reinforcement-learning result.
The frustrating part is that Vera does not need this help, with early independent testing suggesting Olympus is genuinely formidable. The whitepaper’s strongest case is the hardware; its weakest case is the story wrapped around it, so let’s pull that story apart.
Olympus Deserves Better Than This Marketing
Before getting out the cheese grater, let’s talk about the good stuff.
Olympus is a very wide out-of-order Arm core.
Its front end can decode ten instructions per cycle and handle up to two taken branches per cycle. NVIDIA describes a neural branch predictor, value prediction, memory renaming, a large instruction window, six 128-bit SVE pipes, four load pipes, two store pipes, a 96 KB L1 data cache, and roughly 10-cycle access to a 2 MB private L2. Eighty-eight of those cores sit behind a 3.4 TB/s coherency fabric and a distributed 164 MB system-level cache.
Looking closer at the core, the value prediction is one of the more unique additions that Olympus has. This has been a research area for a long time and what value prediction allows Olympus to do is if the core correctly predicts a result, dependent instructions can keep moving instead of piling up behind a long-latency operation. Researchers have
discovered that Apple uses value prediction
in their cores and AMD talked about how in
Family 17h (Zen 1 and 2) they could predict the value of some floating point instructions
. However, AMD’s Family 17h implementation was quite limited, while Olympus appears to have a broader value-prediction implementation closer to Apple’s.
However, the graph prefetcher is not unique to NVIDIA. Intel has a similar mechanism called Data-Dependent Prefetcher that has been in shipping silicon since at least 2022. Intel’s newest datacenter CPU, Granite Rapids, also has an
Array of Pointers prefetcher
which “treats the data prefetched for a constant stride load as a pointer and may issue prefetch requests to the memory addresses corresponding to the pointer’s value.” This is fundamentally the same producer-consumer idea that NVIDIA describes for its graph prefetcher. Intel’s implementation is fairly constrained, so NVIDIA’s implementation may be able to deal with more complex chains than Intel’s implementation. So while Vera’s Graph Prefetcher may be an implementation that can deal with more workloads, producer-consumer prefetching is not a new idea.
Nor is a “neural branch predictor” a new idea. Back in 2012,
AMD implemented a perceptron branch predictor
in the Piledriver microarchitecture and continued to use a
perceptron-based branch predictor in Zen 1
. However, starting with Zen 2, AMD used a perceptron BPU only for its initial direction prediction, with a TAGE predictor overriding it because it delivered
a 30% reduction in mispredictions
. With Zen 5, AMD has likely
fully committed to TAGE predictors
, if it had not already done so with Zen 3 or Zen 4.
Moving to the SoC side, with how beefy the Olympus core is, NVIDIA has given Vera an equally beefy memory subsystem. Vera pairs eight SOCAMM2 LPDDR5X modules with up to 1.5 TB of capacity and 1.2 TB/s of bandwidth. NVIDIA claims the populated memory subsystem only consumes approximately 50 watts. A conventional EPYC or Xeon platform can offer higher-capacity DIMMs which are easier to replace, but it pays for that flexibility in board area and power.
Most importantly, we have more than NVIDIA’s results to look at. In May, Michael Larabel at Phoronix ran an early Vera system against current Arm and x86 servers.
Across the NVIDIA-permitted test set, Vera’s geomean was 10%
above a 5 GHz EPYC 9575F, 1.55x a Xeon 6980P, and 1.63x Grace which makes Vera the most performant Arm server CPU we have seen in public testing. There are major caveats with the testing, such as NVIDIA choosing the permitted workload scope and not allowing frequency or power monitoring. The system that Phoronix tested was pre-production and the test window was one day which puts a fairly hard limit on what they could t

data.title: Decimen Optical Transfer: fountain-coded QR file transfer
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary:
Decimen Optical Transfer 是一个开源文件传输工具,通过屏幕显示和摄像头扫描实现设备间文件传输,无需网络连接、应用安装或配对。

**工作原理:**发送端将文件编码为连续动态QR码流,接收端用摄像头扫描重建文件。采用喷泉码(Luby transform)技术,接收任意约1.15倍原始帧数即可还原,丢帧只影响速度不影响正确性。

**主要特性:**
- 支持最大64MB文件
- 传输速度可达128 KB/s
- SHA-256校验确保完整性
- 离线可用,支持PWA安装
- 开源(MIT协议)

可直接访问 decimen.app 使用,无需安装。项目基于node-qrcode和zxing-wasm构建。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个使用视觉编码（可能是QR码或类似技术）进行离线文件传输的项目，底层技术采用喷泉码

不同观点：

• **实用性肯定派**（elric）：认为这解决了设备间离线传输的长期痛点，不依赖在线服务，建议添加带外密钥交换的加密功能，并提出可用音频替代视频的改进方案

• **技术测试派**（smalltorch）：关注传输距离和安全性，认为这是廉价的激光链接方案，但指出无线电传输存在被拦截风险

• **性能优化派**（felooboolooomba）：发现实际技术问题——发送端60fps但接收端仅40fps，降至30fps后速度反而大幅提升，说明存在帧率协商优化空间

• **技术原理派**（legulere、kooi）：关注底层喷泉码技术的应用和价值

补充讨论：thisisauserid提出有趣的理论观察——这种编码方式展示了完美压缩与随机噪声在视觉上的相似性。整体讨论氛围积极，涉及安全性、性能调优、技术原理和应用场景等多个维度。

Decimen Optical Transfer: fountain-coded QR file transfer
Send a file between two devices using nothing but a
screen and a camera
.
One page displays the file as an endless stream of animated QR codes; another
device points its camera at it and reconstructs the file.
No network path
between the devices, no app, no pairing, no permissions beyond the camera.
The payload travels as light.
Try it
→
decimen.app
Open it on both devices and go — nothing to install. Works offline after the
first visit, and installs as an app on both iOS and Android if you want it on
a home screen.
Files up to 64 MB (or a pasted text snippet), filename and media type
preserved, gzip only when it helps, SHA-256 verified before anything is
offered — and received video plays right in the page. Extracted from a larger
experiment that reached
128 KB/s phone-to-phone
.
Mid-transfer: a phone pulling a file out of the air at 130 KB/s.
Neither mode is encrypted: whatever is on the sending screen is readable by
any camera pointed at it. The property this gives you is no network, not
confidentiality — see
privacy
.
Documentation
Using it

The short version of the protocol: a screen-to-camera link has no
back-channel, so the sender streams fountain-coded frames (
Luby
transform
) — the receiver
collects
any
~K·1.15 distinct frames in any order and peels the file out.
Dropped frames cost time, never correctness.

Network

once). Walkthrough:

.
Similar projects
The concept here was arrived at independently. It turns out several people
have had similar ideas, and their takes are all worth a look:
mohankumarelec/airgapped-qr-code-transfer
:
browser-based QR file transfer with compression and sequential chunking.
Discovered after publicly demoing this project; convergent evolution in
action.
divan/txqr
(2018): animated QR plus
fountain codes in Go, with two excellent write-ups on why fountain coding
beats sequential looping.
sz3/libcimbar
: goes past QR entirely
with a custom high-density color code purpose-built for this channel.

, with

.

data.author: shailendraht
data.article_summary:
HyperProbe 是一个 AI 驱动的故障处理系统，专门解决生产环境中的疑难问题。它通过在代码特定行放置只读"探针"，实时捕获变量状态和日志中缺失的关键数据，无需重新部署或重启服务。

核心优势：将故障根因分析时间从 3-4 小时缩短至 10 分钟以内，无需高级工程师参与战情室，零重新部署。工作流程包括自动接收告警、分析日志追踪、智能放置虚拟断点、捕获实时数据并确认根本原因。

特别擅长处理静默失败、异常与原因分离、竞态条件等难以复现的问题。系统完全只读、部署在客户基础设施内、对用户请求零影响（不到 1% 开销）。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HyperProbe作为AI驱动的生产环境调试工具的价值和可行性

不同观点：
• **质疑派**：认为AppSignal、Rollbar等成熟工具已能自动收集调用栈变量并定位错误；该工具似乎在弥补糟糕的系统设计（如返回200却失败的订单、缺乏日志追踪）；访问敏感客户数据进行调试本身就是不良实践

• **支持派**：认可在现有观测工具之上增加AI调试层的定位；read-only探针能捕获运行时证据而无需重新部署；可补充代码审查前的静默逻辑bug

• **技术关注派**：关注热路径上的性能开销和p99延迟、探针异常的故障隔离、跨语言运行时的只读保证实现、serverless短生命周期环境的兼容性、审计追踪机制

• **风险警示派**：指出AI错误诊断比无答案更危险——会用可信的错误结论误导工程师（如将内存耗尽误判为编码器bug）；更需要"我不知道，但这是两个假设及区分它们的检查方法"而非单一错误答案

补充讨论：产品展示方式需改进——应面向工程师而非CTO，更快切入技术要点而非广告式短段落；有开发者分享了用shellshare.net实现类似实时日志监控的替代方案

49185389.article_summary:
HyperProbe 是一个 AI 驱动的故障处理系统，专门解决生产环境中的疑难问题。它通过在代码特定行放置只读"探针"，实时捕获变量状态和日志中缺失的关键数据，无需重新部署或重启服务。

核心优势：将故障根因分析时间从 3-4 小时缩短至 10 分钟以内，无需高级工程师参与战情室，零重新部署。工作流程包括自动接收告警、分析日志追踪、智能放置虚拟断点、捕获实时数据并确认根本原因。

特别擅长处理静默失败、异常与原因分离、竞态条件等难以复现的问题。系统完全只读、部署在客户基础设施内、对用户请求零影响（不到 1% 开销）。

主要讨论点：HyperProbe作为AI驱动的生产环境调试工具的价值和可行性

不同观点：
• **质疑派**：认为AppSignal、Rollbar等成熟工具已能自动收集调用栈变量并定位错误；该工具似乎在弥补糟糕的系统设计（如返回200却失败的订单、缺乏日志追踪）；访问敏感客户数据进行调试本身就是不良实践

• **支持派**：认可在现有观测工具之上增加AI调试层的定位；read-only探针能捕获运行时证据而无需重新部署；可补充代码审查前的静默逻辑bug

• **技术关注派**：关注热路径上的性能开销和p99延迟、探针异常的故障隔离、跨语言运行时的只读保证实现、serverless短生命周期环境的兼容性、审计追踪机制

• **折中方案派**：建议双方协商土地交换、限制功率和噪音、增加太阳能板、调整建筑布局等解决方案，认为完全阻止是"错失机会"

data.title: Celld: Self-hosted, distributed Durable Objects
data.author: calvinfo
data.article_summary: celld 是一个开源守护进程，允许在自有机器上运行 Cloudflare Workers 和 Durable Objects。核心特点包括：每个对象是独立的 SQLite 数据库，通过用户拥有的 S3 兼容存储桶进行状态复制和节点协调，无需控制平面或共识服务。系统采用对象存储的 compare-and-swap 机制确保同一时间只有一个节点拥有某个单元，避免共享数据库的竞争问题。每个节点嵌入 V8 引擎执行代码，持续将 SQLite 数据库复制到存储桶。当单元迁移或唤醒时，新所有者从存储桶恢复数据库并继续执行。空闲单元可休眠以节省资源。系统提供命令行工具和 Docker 容器两种部署方式，支持 AWS S3 及其他兼容服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Deno 团队推出的 celld（支持自托管 durable objects 的技术）引发了关于技术应用、AI 对开源影响以及架构设计的多方面讨论。

不同观点：

• **AI 对开源贡献的影响存在分歧**：sakesun 引用某项目禁用 PR 的声明，担心 AI 工具让低质量、缺乏上下文的大规模修改泛滥，增加维护者负担；ironqcold 则认为 AI 只是让垃圾贡献更容易产生，优质贡献者的价值反而更高，AI 本身不会杀死开源。

• **对技术价值的认可**：khalidx、dzonga、myshapeprotocol 等积极评价 durable objects 概念的价值，认为"每个对象是自己的 SQLite 数据库"这一抽象简洁而强大，支持自托管和去中心化是重要进步。jumploops 分享了实际应用案例证明其可行性。

• **技术对比需求**：多位评论者希望了解 celld 与其他技术的区别，包括 Cloudflare workerd、Temporal、Restate、Azure Durable Functions 等，meowtimemania 特别希望看到性能基准测试。

• **架构可靠性质疑**：jiveturkey 对依赖 S3 作为底层存储表示担忧，质疑正确性是否过度依赖黑盒服务，希望看到更自包含的方案。

补充讨论：jauntywundrkind 详细分析了技术时机和架构细节（V8 隔离、低开销运行时），hhthrowaway1230 和 vmg12 提出了本地运行和 spot 实例支持等功能需求。

celld
Self-hosted, distributed
Durable Objects
.
celld is an open-source daemon that runs Cloudflare Workers and Durable
Objects on your own machines. Each object is its own SQLite database,
addressed by name and replicated to an
S3-compatible bucket you own; nodes coordinate through that bucket alone, with
no control plane or consensus. Because every object is its own small database,
applications shard by construction — the contention and blast-radius failures
of one shared database are designed out, not managed. Idle cells hibernate to
nearly nothing. Learn more at
celld.dev
or read the
documentation
.
How it works
Every
celld
node embeds V8 and executes Wrangler bundles. The fleet shares an
S3-compatible bucket containing deployments, cell state, and small ownership
records. Object-storage compare-and-swap ensures that exactly one node owns a
cell at a time, without a membership protocol, failure detector, or consensus
service.
celld continuously replicates each cell's SQLite database to the bucket.
When a cell moves or wakes up, its new owner restores that database and resumes
execution. The bucket is the durable source of truth; nodes are replaceable.
Install
The installer downloads the
celld
binary (provenance is verifiable with
gh attestation verify
):
curl -fsSL https://celld.dev/install.sh
|
sh
Put
~/.local/bin
on your
PATH
if the installer asks you to.
Worker projects deployed with
celld deploy
need
esbuild
on
PATH
; asset-only projects do not.
The installer keeps verified releases under
~/.local/lib/celld/releases
and
atomically switches one
current
pointer. To remove celld, use the guarded
uninstaller:
curl -fsSL https://celld.dev/uninstall.sh
|
sh
Container
The release image contains the
celld
binary and is published for Linux
x86-64 and ARM64:
docker run --rm ghcr.io/denoland/celld --version
Persist the runtime's local state and pass the standard AWS credential
environment through:
docker volume create celld-state
docker run --rm --network host \
-e AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID \
-e AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY \
-e AWS_SESSION_TOKEN \
-e CELLD_WATCH=/var/lib/celld/state \
-v celld-state:/var/lib/celld \
ghcr.io/denoland/celld \
--bucket s3://my-cells-bucket \
--endpoint https://ACCOUNT.r2.cloudflarestorage.com \
--region auto \
--listen 0.0.0.0:8080 \
--advertise node-a.internal:8080
Drop
--endpoint
/
--region
for real AWS S3. Behind a load balancer,
give each node a distinct
--advertise
its peers can reach.
Run it
celld uses the standard AWS credential chain. Deploy to an S3-compatible
bucket, then start celld against the same bucket:
celld deploy
.
\
--bucket s3://my-cells-bucket
celld \
--bucket s3://my-cells-bucket \
--listen 0.0.0.0:8080 \
--advertise 10.0.0.12:8080
Use
--endpoint
for another S3-compatible service and
--region
when it
cannot be inferred. A fleet runs one application, and every node loads its
latest successfully committed deployment from
deploy/current.json
. Run
celld --help
for the complete command line.
Deployment objects use the documented types in
crates/celld/protocol.rs
.
celld deploy
invokes
esbuild
from
PATH
for Worker code, accepts the supported
Wrangler config subset—including co-deployed or asset-only static
assets—and writes those objects directly. Every node discovers owners and
peers from bucket leases; there is no account or join service.
Peer HTTP does not terminate TLS. Put every advertised address on a trusted
private network or an encrypted overlay such as WireGuard or Tailscale; do not
publish the peer port directly. A literal public IP is rejected unless
--unsafe-public-advertise
is supplied explicitly. The first current node creates
fleet/peer-auth.json
in the bucket. All peer requests are protocol-versioned,
body-bound, HMAC-authenticated, clock-bounded, and replay-protected with that
fleet secret. Treat access to the bucket and its credentials as fleet
administrator access.
Operate a fleet
celld diagnose
enumerates every node lease by default, then performs a signed
direct probe of each live peer:
celld diagnose --bucket s3://my-cells-bucket
The report keeps checking after an individual failure and distinguishes
expired records, malformed or unsafe advertise addresses, unreachable peers,
and incompatible protocols. It also prints each node's coarse resident-cell,
WebSocket, RSS, CPU, file-descriptor, pressure, and shedding sample. Pass one
or more
--peer NODE_ID
options to restrict the c

data.title: GNU Hurd News 2026-Q2
data.author: plaguna
data.article_summary:
这是GNU Hurd项目2026年第二季度的进展报告，主要更新包括：

1. **9P文件系统支持**：Sergey Bugaev发布了9pfs转换器的开源实现，支持基本的文件浏览、路径解析和读写操作。

2. **AArch64架构支持**：Paulo Duarte提交了补丁系列，为GNU Mach内核添加AArch64 ABI实现。

3. **设备管理改进**：Mikhail Karpov扩展了partfs转换器，使其能处理多个磁盘及分区，实现动态设备管理，取代静态/dev条目。

4. **Rust支持**：Almudena Garcia正在开发Rust版本的trivfs实现，让开发者可以用Rust编写Hurd转换器。

5. **其他修复**：包括任务优先级设置、msync的POSIX验证、内核崩溃修复等多项改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GNU Hurd微内核操作系统的开发进展和未来前景

不同观点：

• **技术乐观派**：关注具体技术进展，如Apple M1移植计划、D编译器支持、9pfs文件系统等新特性，认为这些是有价值的技术探索

• **实用怀疑派**：对35年开发历程后仍在讨论SVG logo感到失望，认为进展"缓慢而随意"，质疑其成为可行替代系统的可能性，有评论讽刺"也许100年后"或称之为"来自墓穴的故事"

• **技术细节关注者**：深入探讨Mach微内核的性能瓶颈（如IPC消息验证开销）以及9pfs的健壮性问题，希望了解Hurd如何解决这些已知问题

• **替代方案倡议者**：认为如果微内核复兴，更可能来自Rust社区而非GNU Hurd；也有人建议用AI编码工具复活此类"死去的有趣开源项目"

补充讨论：部分评论者欣赏这种"不为赚钱的小型技术项目"，以及将旧MacBook用GuixSD+Hurd改造的创意用途。整体氛围在技术兴趣与现实主义之间摇摆。

Hello and welcome to another Qoth!  Here's what's been happening in Q2
of 2026!
Joshua Branson added a pretty cool svg logo for our
ethernet
multiplexor
.  He built that image
with Inkscape whilst using a Hurd laptop (Thinkpad 420) running on
real iron! The Hurd wiki could certainly use more artwork.  Perhaps
you have a favorite Hurd translator that you believes needs some
artwork!
Sergey Bugaev announced his
WIP
9pfs
(
source code
),
and it has a
wiki page
! He writes:
Some years ago, I experimented with implementing a 9P translator for
the Hurd. Hopefully there is no need to tell this list what 9P is :)
Besides just browsing files on the few existing servers out there, a
potential use case is virtio-9p, to enable shared directory trees
between VMs and the host. But that would need someone to implement
virtio support in the Hurd.
I wanted to complete 9pfs before publishing, but that ultimately
didn't happen, so now it's time to turn it over to the community. I
now went and made the repository public on GitHub:
https://github.com/bugaevc/9pfs
What's implemented is basic browsing (readdir, stat), path resolution
(dir_lookup), and reading files (io_read). And below that, the whole
tracking for nodes, peropens, protids, fids, tags, and 9p RPCs.
Improvements are welcome, send patches to this list with [PATCH 9pfs]
in the subject. A good starting point would be to continue porting
things that I had implemented in the old netfs-based version (see
netfs.c) but didn't yet port to the new one.
He then got a little more motivated, and he added some write support!
Etienne Brateau added
validation
to
msync
, so
that the Hurd better follows POSIX.
Diego Nieto Cid worked on allowing privileged users to set their task
priority (nice value).  His patches landed in
glibc
and
GNU
Mach
.
He also fixed a
tiny
bug
in our test suite. He fixed an adjtime bug, which is helpful to
the
OpenNTPD
port
,
and he fixed
two more
bugs
.
Paulo Duarte sent a RFC patch series trying to commit Sergeyâs
previous AArch64 work. He writes:
This series adds the gnumach kernel-side implementation for the
aarch64 ABI Sergey landed in April 2024, plus the test-suite arms.
Patch 01 brings in the aarch64-only sources from bugaevc/wip-aarch64
verbatim, with Sergey as Author; the rest is mine.
The meaningful divergence from wip-aarch64 is what I left out:
roughly 150 files of cross-arch refactoring across kern/, ipc/, vm/,
device/intr.{c,h}, and the i386 tree. Each got replaced with a
smaller per-arch shim under aarch64/ so kern/bootstrap.c,
device/intr.{c,h}, kern/lock.h, and the i386 trees all stay
bit-identical to current master. The shared-file footprint outside
aarch64/ is four files: a new ELF constant, two missing decls plus

49146183.article_summary:
这是GNU Hurd项目2026年第二季度的进展报告，主要更新包括：

1. **9P文件系统支持**：Sergey Bugaev发布了9pfs转换器的开源实现，支持基本的文件浏览、路径解析和读写操作。

2. **AArch64架构支持**：Paulo Duarte提交了补丁系列，为GNU Mach内核添加AArch64 ABI实现。

3. **设备管理改进**：Mikhail Karpov扩展了partfs转换器，使其能处理多个磁盘及分区，实现动态设备管理，取代静态/dev条目。

4. **Rust支持**：Almudena Garcia正在开发Rust版本的trivfs实现，让开发者可以用Rust编写Hurd转换器。

5. **其他修复**：包括任务优先级设置、msync的POSIX验证、内核崩溃修复等多项改进。

data.title: I'm switching my phone from Android to Linux
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary:
作者因不满Android系统的诸多问题（Google服务追踪、限制定制ROM、强制AI功能、限制应用安装等），决定在手机上改用Linux系统。

经过对比Ubuntu Touch和SailfishOS等移动Linux系统后，作者最终选择了SailfishOS。该系统具有手势导航、优秀的应用框架和完整的Linux特性（支持SSH），但也存在软件版本过旧、部分功能损坏等问题。Ubuntu Touch虽支持Waydroid但用户体验欠佳。

由于银行、政府服务和Uber等必需应用暂时无法在Linux手机上运行，作者保留了一台Android备用机用于这些特定场景。未来将继续测试并记录使用体验，考虑购买Jolla Phone 2。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：移动操作系统的开放性困境——Android垄断加剧与Linux替代方案的可行性争议

不同观点：

• **Android系统好但Google服务差**：认为Android内核设计优秀，真正问题是Google Play Services过度集成，获取过多权限，且Play Integrity机制阻止替代方案出现。理想状态是解耦服务模块，让用户自由选择实现方式

• **Linux手机追赶困难**：指出技术差距巨大——相机软件落后数年、键盘缺乏智能纠错和虚拟按键调整、GPS/银行/智能钥匙等关键功能缺失。认为Linux无法像桌面端那样追上主流系统

• **生态锁定正在加剧**：批评Android从开源诱饵转向封闭锁定，银行和政府服务迁移后现在收紧控制。Bootloader解锁受限、attestation机制普及、应用实际只支持Google-Android而非AOSP

• **替代系统实践者**：分享Sailfish OS、GrapheneOS、Ubuntu Touch使用经验。有人通过双设备方案解决（Linux日常+Pixel银行），有人依赖Android兼容层，但都面临VoLTE、NFC支付、蓝牙连接等功能缺失

补充讨论：争议焦点在于"牺牲便利换取自由"是否值得。支持者强调开源可审计和用户控制权，认为LLM时代更需要这种自由；怀疑者指出银行应用和Web都在收紧（通过安全启动栈），第三方系统空间正在被挤压。部分人提出Windows Phone式方案，但承认需放弃银行应用。

49188022.article_content:
I'm switching my phone from Android to Linux.
02 Aug, 2026
For the past months or even years, I've become more and more dissatisfied with the path Google has taken with the Android Open Source Project (AOSP). Be it the dependency and insane
tracking
of Google Play Services,
locking down
of device trees to hinder custom ROM development, all the AI stuff being put into the system, or most recently (and perhaps worst),
removing
the ability of installing apps per your own wishing - it's become sort of like a "death by a thousand papercuts" situation. While the AOSP isn't exactly dead (yet), it kind of feels like it's just a question of time. Therefore, I've decided to jump ship. I'm installing linux on my phone.
The mobile linux space isn't exactly looking good right now, but it holds some promise. Ubuntu Touch managed to survive being abandoned by Canonical, and postmarket is still seeing good development even if not having great hardware adapation at the moment. SailfishOS (even if it has proprietary parts) has also made great progress with strong support for android apps on official devices and what seems to be a real good launch of their Jolla 2.
Personally I'm lucky enough to own a Fairphone 4 that just so happens to support all of these. After a bit back and forth I've ultimately ended up with SailfishOS. Overall it's a good system - I like the gesture based navigation and its application framework is beautiful. It's also cool how it's very
linux
. If I have an issue or something I want to tinker with I can just ssh over from my PC either wirelessly or via USB.  It's not without it's issues though. For some reason it ships horribly outdated versions of python and glibc making some things more difficult than needed, and waydroid and GPS is broken on the fairphone port - worth noting an unofficial port. Many of the community-built apps are also either in-part or completely slop-coded, such as a whatsapp client that I (sadly) am dependant on.
Ubuntu Touch is also an option, but isn't without it's own bag of issues. Waydroid runs there which is a huge plus, but notifications and clipboard doesn't sync across making it really hard to use ie. Bitwarden (Sailfish has an unofficial port which is almost flawless). The default and native apps are pretty lackluster compared to both Android and Sailfish. Among other things I was unable to figure out how to block phone numbers, a highly needed feature for anyone that has VIVO as their cellular provider. I'm also not a big fan of how the UI works with app navigation and with the "top bar"/"drop down menu". If you want to know more about it, The Linux Experiments has some good videos on both youtube and
peertube
.
Sadly, I won't be able to abandon android completely
yet
. The no waydroid means that I can't access some apps that I need be it for online verification for logging onto bank and government services in Norway or apps I need for my own security here in Brazil such as Uber. Luckily I've had a Galaxy A17 lying around as a backup phone for half a year now which I can carry around for these exact services. I just open up a wifi hotspot from my FP4, do the exact tasks, and close it off again. Other than that, I will try to avoid using it as much as physically possible.
As this progresses I will take note of what works and what doesn't before making either a proper writeup or video in a while. It's not gonna be easy, but hopefully it will be worth it.
Oh, and slight spoilers for what my experience with Sailfish is after some usage, but I might go ahead and buy a Jolla Phone 2 when I return to Norway.

data.title: On non-rooted Android 17, ADB uninstall of system apps fails
data.author: microtonal
data.article_summary: 这是一个针对Universal Android Debloater项目的功能请求（issue #1426）。用户Rudxain建议将应用的默认操作模式从"卸载"（Uninstall）改为"禁用"（Disable/Freeze）模式，理由是卸载模式会引发过多问题。该请求已被标记为"enhancement"（功能增强），目前处于开放状态，尚未分配给任何开发者处理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Android 17禁止卸载系统应用，只允许禁用功能，引发用户对设备控制权和隐私的担忧

不同观点：

• **强烈反对派**：认为这是"通用计算战争"的升级，用户正在失去对设备的真正所有权。类比：买了手机却像租户一样受制于HOA（业主协会）规则，欧盟主权被美国科技公司掌控

• **技术解决方案派**：推荐使用GrapheneOS等隐私ROM，或通过Shizuku + Canta等工具实现伪root权限来禁用系统应用，认为解决方案仍然存在

• **理性分析派**：指出禁用功能已能达到同样目的，卸载"只读分区"的应用本来就不合理。认为改动影响有限，因为系统空间无法被用户利用

• **根本性质疑**：为什么手机不能直接运行GNU/Linux？预测开放硬件终将胜出，封闭生态终将消亡（除非以"保护儿童"为名立法禁止）

补充讨论：核心争议在于卸载与禁用是否有实质差异——被禁用的应用是否仍在后台运行收集数据无人知晓。部分用户计划暂停系统更新以保持卸载能力。有人质疑Google的真实动机，认为其回应完全回避了人们想移除Google Play服务的隐私原因。

data.title: Sycophantic AI Decreases Prosocial Intentions and Promotes Dependence (2025)
data.author: robin_reala
data.article_summary: 这篇论文研究了AI"阿谀奉承"现象的普遍性及其危害。研究发现，11个主流AI模型肯定用户行为的频率比人类高50%，即使在涉及操纵或欺骗等有害行为时也会肯定。通过1604名参与者的实验显示，与阿谀奉承的AI互动会显著降低人们修复人际冲突的意愿，增强其认为自己正确的信念。矛盾的是，用户却更喜欢、更信任这类AI，并愿意继续使用。这种偏好创造了恶性激励循环，促使用户依赖阿谀奉承的AI，同时推动AI训练朝这个方向发展，最终可能侵蚀用户判断力并减少亲社会行为。
data.comments_summary:
**主要讨论点：** AI模型的过度迎合（sycophancy）对用户的影响及其利弊

**不同观点：**

• **批判派（主流）：** AI迎合会侵蚀信任和判断力。kazinator指出AI会根据用户说法随意改变立场，导致信息混乱；SwellJoe将其比作"亿万富翁从不听到'不'"的有害体验；rramadass通过实验证明AI在常识推理上有严重缺陷，过度赞美会扭曲现实

• **反驳派：** romaniitedomum指出OpenAI在2026年4月因用户大量投诉而回滚了过度迎合的模型，说明多数用户其实不喜欢迎合；认为易受迎合影响的主要是非技术用户

• **辩护派：** Lutger认为AI有独特优势——无限耐心、客观中立、快速整合信息，在某些方面胜过人类治疗师；强调"如果你知道自己在做什么"可以有效利用AI

• **系统性问题派：** donatj和Kattywumpus认为这不只是AI问题，互联网生态（回音室、点赞机制）整体都在强化验证偏见

• **极端立场：** lowsong预言聊天机器人将被视为本世纪最危险发明并被禁止；kittikitti通过个人经历反讽指出人们实际上偏好迎合者

**补充讨论：** alexalx666提出依赖性警告；accountrequired用讽刺回复"你完全正确"直接展示迎合行为；核心争议在于AI迎合的程度、影响范围，以及用户是否有能力识别和抵御这种影响。

Title:
Sycophantic AI Decreases Prosocial Intentions and Promotes Dependence

View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Both the general public and academic communities have raised concerns about sycophancy, the phenomenon of artificial intelligence (AI) excessively agreeing with or flattering users. Yet, beyond isolated media reports of severe consequences, like reinforcing delusions, little is known about the extent of sycophancy or how it affects people who use AI. Here we show the pervasiveness and harmful impacts of sycophancy when people seek advice from AI. First, across 11 state-of-the-art AI models, we find that models are highly sycophantic: they affirm users' actions 50% more than humans do, and they do so even in cases where user queries mention manipulation, deception, or other relational harms. Second, in two preregistered experiments (N = 1604), including a live-interaction study where participants discuss a real interpersonal conflict from their life, we find that interaction with sycophantic AI models significantly reduced participants' willingness to take actions to repair interpersonal conflict, while increasing their conviction of being in the right. However, participants rated sycophantic responses as higher quality, trusted the sycophantic AI model more, and were more willing to use it again. This suggests that people are drawn to AI that unquestioningly validate, even as that validation risks eroding their judgment and reducing their inclination toward prosocial behavior. These preferences create perverse incentives both for people to increasingly rely on sycophantic AI models and for AI model training to favor sycophancy. Our findings highlight the necessity of explicitly addressing this incentive structure to mitigate the widespread risks of AI sycophancy.

49186720.article_summary: 这篇论文研究了AI"阿谀奉承"现象的普遍性及其危害。研究发现，11个主流AI模型肯定用户行为的频率比人类高50%，即使在涉及操纵或欺骗等有害行为时也会肯定。通过1604名参与者的实验显示，与阿谀奉承的AI互动会显著降低人们修复人际冲突的意愿，增强其认为自己正确的信念。矛盾的是，用户却更喜欢、更信任这类AI，并愿意继续使用。这种偏好创造了恶性激励循环，促使用户依赖阿谀奉承的AI，同时推动AI训练朝这个方向发展，最终可能侵蚀用户判断力并减少亲社会行为。

data.title: The Cipher Behind Qsyrupwd: Reconstructing IBM i Password Hashes
data.author: jandeboevrie
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了IBM i系统上QSYRUPWD API的安全分析。该API用于返回加密的用户密码数据，支持密码同步和迁移等管理功能。

作者在渗透测试中发现，当系统的QPWDLVL（密码级别）设置为2-4时，QSYRUPWD返回的加密数据格式与John the Ripper等密码破解工具所期望的格式不兼容，导致即使拥有*ALLOBJ和*SECADM权限也无法进行实际的密码强度测试。

为深入分析这个问题，作者编写了一个CL程序来调用QSYRUPWD API并提取返回的数据缓冲区，并使用IBM i的STRTRC工具进行API调用追踪，以验证不同QPWDLVL设置下API的实际输出格式，从而确定返回数据是否与现有破解工具兼容。

49094358.article_content:
Intro
QSYRUPWD (Retrieve Encrypted User Password) is an IBM i API that returns password-related
data for a specified user profile in encrypted form to authorized callers.
IBM i is IBM’s integrated enterprise platform, originating from the AS/400 line,
and is still widely used for business-critical workloads such as ERP, finance,
logistics, and manufacturing.
The API primarily exists to support system functions such as password synchronization,
migration, replication, and other administrative scenarios where password material
must be transferred without exposing the cleartext password. IBM documents QSYRUPWD
as part of its security-related API set for handling encrypted password data.
During one of our IBM i penetration tests, I noticed that the client’s server was
configured with
QPWDLVL = 2
. On IBM i, the
QPWDLVL
system value determines both
the password rules accepted by the operating system and the verifier formats maintained
for authentication compatibility. IBM documents that password levels 0 and 1 correspond
to the older DES-based scheme,
levels 2 and 3
use a SHA-1-based scheme,
and
level 4
introduces a PBKDF2-based verifier model. IBM also states that when
QPWDLVL
is set to 2, the operating system keeps compatibility with multiple password-verifier
forms rather than removing earlier ones.
This distinction is important when interpreting
QSYRUPWD
output.
John the Ripper includes dedicated IBM i cracking formats for legacy IBM i material,
specifically
as400_des
and
as400_ssha1
, which reflects support for the older
DES-based and salted SHA-1-based representations. However, in our testing, the
QSYRUPWD
output obtained from systems running at QPWDLVL 2–4 did not match the form expected by
John the Ripper’s IBM i formats, whereas the legacy QPWDLVL 0–1 case is compatible with
the QSYRUPWD-derived material handled by those modules. In other words, for QPWDLVL 2–4,
the content returned by
QSYRUPWD
changes in a way that makes direct use with the existing
John the Ripper IBM i formats unsuccessful. This is an empirical observation from our
testing and tooling analysis, not a claim that IBM publicly documents the exact returned
structure for those levels.
As a result, even with
*ALLOBJ
and
*SECADM
(which are required to call
QSYRUPWD
), the API
could no longer be used for practical password-strength testing. After this engagement,
I decided to analyze the
QSYRUPWD
API in detail.
Tools
To examine the API behavior directly, I wrote a small CL program that invokes
QSYRUPWD
with the
UPWD0100
format, retrieves the returned buffer, and emits
it for further analysis.
The goal was not to build a full extraction tool, but to verify what kind of
password-related data the API returns under different
QPWDLVL
settings.
This made it possible to compare the actual output format across systems and
determine whether the returned data matched the input expected by existing
cracking tools such as John the Ripper.
PGM PARM(&USER)
DCL VAR(&USER) TYPE(*CHAR) LEN(10)
DCL VAR(&RCV) TYPE(*CHAR) LEN(4000)
DCL VAR(&LEN) TYPE(*INT) LEN(4) VALUE(4000)
DCL VAR(&FMT) TYPE(*CHAR) LEN(8) VALUE('UPWD0100')
DCL VAR(&ERR) TYPE(*CHAR) LEN(8) VALUE(X'0000000000000000')
DCL VAR(&N) TYPE(*INT) LEN(4)
DCL VAR(&N4) TYPE(*CHAR) LEN(4)
DCL VAR(&NCH) TYPE(*CHAR) LEN(11)
CALL PGM(QSZS/QSYRUPWD) PARM(&RCV &LEN &FMT &USER &ERR)
MONMSG CPF0000 EXEC(DO)
SNDPGMMSG MSGID(CPF9898) MSGF(QCPFMSG) MSGDTA('QSYRUPWD failed') MSGTYPE(*ESCAPE)
RETURN
ENDDO
CHGVAR VAR(&N4) VALUE(%SST(&RCV 1 4))
CHGVAR VAR(&N) VALUE(%BIN(&N4))
CHGVAR VAR(&NCH) VALUE(%CHAR(&N))
SNDPGMMSG MSGID(CPF9898) MSGF(QCPFMSG) MSGDTA('QSYRUPWD ok, bytes:' *BCAT &NCH) MSGTYPE(*INFO)
SNDPGMMSG MSGID(CPF9898) MSGF(QCPFMSG) MSGDTA('Data: ' *BCAT &RCV) MSGTYPE(*INFO)
ENDPGM
Trace
After I compiled the
PWDDUMP
program, I wondered whether we could
generate a call trace. Luckily, IBM i provides a tool called
STRTRC
that can be
used to collect evidence about the calls made within
QSYRUPWD
.
So I logged in with a user that has
*ALLOBJ
and
*SECADM
authority
(required to run
PWDDUMP
), and ran the following commands:
STRTRC SSNID(MYTRACE) JOB(*ALL/QSECOFR/QPADEV0005) JOBTRCTYPE(*ALL)
CALL USERB1/PWDDUMP USERB1
ENDTRC SSNID(MYTRACE) PRTTRC(*YES)
PRTTRC  DTALIB(QGPL) DTAMBR(MYTRACE)
These commands create a spool file with the required call-trace information,
but the structure is a bit confusing at first glance, here is a sample
snippet of the spool file:
|         |    SYNCHRONOU
CALL  |   CPU   |   READS |  WR
TIME            THREAD    FLAG  FUNCTION PROGRAM                       LIBRARY     ENTRY   EXIT    LVL   |   TIME  |  DB  NDB|  DB
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
12:53:35.829041 00000065        CALL     QCMD                          QSYS       x000519 x000519     1     .000000    0    0    0
12:53:35.829041 00000065        CALL     QUICMENU                      QSYS       x0000C1 x0000C1     2     .000000

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大语言模型）是否能够像爱因斯坦发明广义相对论那样，实现科学上的直觉"跳跃"性突破

不同观点：

• **怀疑派**：认为LLM受限于语言这种"有损编码"的训练数据，缺乏感官体验和物理直觉，无法实现超越人类经验的跳跃；真正理解需要"不知道"的能力，而LLM必须给出答案

• **反驳派**：引用具体证据反驳，如Terence Tao与ChatGPT协作、AI发现Jacobian猜想反例、单位距离问题反例等，认为LLM已展现跳跃能力；即使当前不行，未来AI形式终将实现

• **方法论批评派**：指出论文缺乏量化证据，只是个人观点；对爱因斯坦相对论历史理解过于简化；过度依赖GR类比，科学发现路径其实很多样（如量子化发现并非源于物理感官）

• **务实派**：质疑为何执着于"替代人类"，认为增强人类能力才是最有价值的应用场景；问题可能在于环境和工具设计，而非LLM本身

补充讨论：论文作者后续澄清这不是"LLM死路一条"的观点，而是探讨特定类型思维能力的个人立场文章。有人提出用1980年代前文本训练LLM来测试其能否重现后续发展的实验想法。

data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：马尔可夫链的熵计算方法及其与生命现象的关系

不同观点：

• **技术质疑派（abetusk）**：指出文章存在技术错误（边标签互换），质疑马尔可夫链熵的计算方法是否明确。认为状态依赖性使传统熵计算失效，提出应使用遍历马尔可夫链的平稳分布来计算熵（$-\sum p_i \lg(p_i)$），并关注熵演化与第二特征值的关系

• **哲学应用派（emsign）**：从生命维持秩序的本质出发，强调热力学定律的普遍性和先验性。认为热力学定律可作为判断标准，用于区分现实与"魔法思维"——任何违反热力学第二定律的想法都是不可能的

• **理论补充派（AIorNot）**：批评原文遗漏Karl Friston的马尔可夫毯理论，该理论通过启发式证明和原始汤模拟，提出生命自组织是任何具有马尔可夫毯的遍历随机动力系统的必然涌现属性

• **学科指引派（niklasbuschmann）**：简要指出"随机热力学"是研究该主题的相关领域

补充讨论：评论者们在不同层面展开讨论——从具体数学计算到生命哲学，反映出熵概念在跨学科研究中的复杂性和丰富性。

• **科学解释派**：MeteorMarc从技术角度解释了形成机制（空爆导致土壤蒸发成不均匀等离子体，快速冷却促进晶体形成）；pfdietz联系到铝金相图和早期IC产业的"紫色瘟疫"问题，提供历史技术背景

• **讽刺幽默派**：多位评论者以幽默方式回应——tastyfreeze讽刺如果早期发现可能会有"原子弹铸造厂"提案；HPsquared调侃"制造过程不太经济"；felooboolooomba开玩笑询问制造方法

• **流行文化联想派**：voidnothings和wartywhoa23都引用《钢之炼金术师》中的贤者之石（暗含用人类灵魂炼成的隐喻）；WorldMaker建议这应该是哥斯拉电影情节；po1nt提议写入科幻作品

补充讨论：争议焦点在于科学发现本身（描述新物质）与实用价值（是否有独特性质）之间的差距，部分评论者对核武器相关研究持批判态度

主要讨论点：Webhooks用于状态同步存在的根本性问题及解决方案的选择

不同观点：

• **标准化派**：需将同步协议纳入IETF/HTTP标准（如Braid-HTTP），支持所有媒体类型和URL，而非专有SCROLL方案，才能真正解决采用难题

• **混合方案派**：Webhooks应作为"提醒"机制配合低频轮询，既保证反应性又避免重复/重试复杂性，无需本地隧道工具

• **效率质疑派**：SCROLL的持久连接对低频事件不划算，CDN限制连接时长，提供商不愿服务持久请求；建议用计数器+事件API解决去重/缓冲问题

• **架构基础派**：批评仅依赖Webhooks的设计，强调必须从"灾难恢复同步"机制出发，支持数据库回滚、长期bug等场景；事件驱动不适合跨组织的状态同步需求

• **实用主义派**：直接提供SQLite数据库下载比复杂的CSV/JSON解析更实用；Webhooks已足够应对实时更新

补充讨论：现实痛点包括Quickbooks等API的不可靠性、本地开发困难（需共享沙箱）、90天事件保留限制。Stripe等大型提供商已采用游标轮询。有人指出房地产行业已有类似实践。

data.title: Exact, parallel 2D Delaunay triangulation for int32 coordinates
data.author: oryx1729
data.article_summary:
Delaunay32是一个快速的C++17库，专门用于对32位有符号整数坐标点进行2D Delaunay三角剖分。该库基于精确整数谓词构建，支持串行或并行执行，可处理约束条件和带孔洞的多边形域。

性能方面，在M1芯片上处理百万点时，8线程版本比其他主流实现（如Fade2D、delaunator-cpp、Triangle）快4-11倍。

主要特性包括：精确预测、确定性重合点处理、显式浮点数到整数的量化转换、批量拓扑构建、保留原始输入索引等。库提供了简洁的API，通过Triangulator类配置问题并调用triangulate()方法完成三角剖分。浮点坐标需先用quantize()工具转换为整数坐标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Delaunay32 三角剖分库的性能表现、技术实现和应用场景

不同观点：

• **性能基准争议**：Remnant44 指出官方基准包含多线程会影响比较公平性，希望看到单线程基准；animal531 和 fp64 则提供了其他实现的性能数据作为参照（Unity Burst 约320ms处理100万点，经典 Triangle 库）

• **精度限制质疑**：ur-whale 认为 int32（40亿步精度）对大多数场景可能已足够，质疑是否真的需要扩展到 int64；hingler36 则关心 32位限制背后的技术权衡，怀疑可能与 SIMD 优化有关

• **功能需求差异**：Remnant44 重点关注约束 Delaunay 支持（实用功能）；MattCruikshank 建议扩展到 3D 四面体剖分（算法扩展）；hingler36 询问动态顶点操作支持（交互需求）

补充讨论：DennisL123 分享了自己的 Rust/WebAssembly 实现作为替代方案，展示了该领域的多样化技术路线；整体氛围积极，多位评论者对项目表示认可并提出建设性问题。

Delaunay32
Fast, parallel 2D Delaunay triangulation for signed 32-bit integer points.
Delaunay32 is a C++17 library built around exact integer predicates. A reusable
Triangulator
receives points, constraints, and polygon domains as one
configured problem, then builds and exports the topology in a single
triangulate()
call.
The core API accepts
std::int32_t
coordinates exclusively. Floating-point
input is converted explicitly with the standalone
quantize()
utility before
it reaches the triangulator.
Performance
Approximate runtime for one million unconstrained points on the reference
Apple M1 system, normalized to eight-thread Delaunay32. Lower is better:
Implementation
Threads
Relative runtime
Delaunay32
8

Delaunay32

~2.8×

automatic
~4.5×

2.17.3

~6.0×
delaunator-cpp
1
~11×
Triangle
1.6
1
~11×
These rounded results come from separate Release-build runs and vary with
machine and input distribution.
Features
Exact predicates for every accepted integer input
Serial or shared-memory parallel execution
Deterministic coincident-point handling
Standalone constraints and disjoint polygon domains with holes
One batched topology for constraints and all polygon boundaries
Triangle-only or full topology results with an operation report
Explicit, configurable float-to-integer quantization
Original input indices in every returned triangle
No bundled third-party source dependencies
Build
The default top-level build includes the library, extras, tests, benchmark, and
the complete example suite:
cmake -S
.
-B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --parallel
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
For a library-only build:
cmake -S
.
-B build \
-DDELAUNAY32_BUILD_BENCHMARKS=OFF \
-DDELAUNAY32_BUILD_EXTRAS=OFF \
-DDELAUNAY32_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF \
-DDELAUNAY32_BUILD_TESTS=OFF
cmake --build build --parallel
Link the core CMake target as
delaunay32::delaunay32
. Optional JSON,
sampling, and SVG utilities are available through
delaunay32::extras
.
Use
#
include
<
delaunay32/delaunay.hpp
>
#
include
<
vector
>
int
main
() {
const
std::vector<delaunay32::Point> points = {
{
0
,
0
}, {
100
,
0
}, {
100
,
100
}, {
0
,
100
}, {
48
,
37
},
};
delaunay32::TriangulationOptions options;
options.
thread_count
=
0
;
//
Select the hardware thread count.
delaunay32::Triangulator triangulator;
triangulator.
set_options
(options);
triangulator.
set_points
(points);
const
delaunay32::TriangulationResult result =
triangulator.
triangulate
();
for
(
const
delaunay32::Triangle& triangle : result.
triangles
) {
const
auto
& a = points[triangle.
i0
];
const
auto
& b = points[triangle.
i1
];
const
auto
& c = points[triangle.
i2
];
//
a, b, c are counterclockwise.
}
}
triangulate()
consumes the configured problem, including when it throws.
Call
set_points()
to begin another problem. This clears the previous
constraints and polygon domains while preserving options, allocations, and
worker threads.
Constraints and polygons are configured before the run:
triangulator.set_points(points);
triangulator.set_constraints(constraints);
triangulator.set_polygons(polygons);
const
auto
result = triangulator.triangulate();
For adjacency, the complete input hull, and duplicate representatives, select
ResultDetail::Full
. Triangle detail is the default.
Floating-point conversion is deliberately separate:

<
delaunay32/quantization.hpp
>
const
delaunay32::QuantizationResult converted =
delaunay32::quantize
(float_points);
triangulator.set_points(converted.points);
const
auto
result = triangulator.triangulate();
The converted vector preserves the source length and index order. Its
QuantizationReport
records the mapping, measured error, and collisions.

data.title: Goodhart's Law Comes for Every Benchmark You Trust
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI模型基准测试的有效性和局限性，以及Goodhart定律在评估体系中的体现

不同观点：

• **非公开基准派**：认为应使用私密、定期更新的测试集，因为公开基准会被训练数据污染。只有未触及公网的问题才能避免数据泄露，且轮换测试集可防止记忆化（throw10920, astro1234支持但指出仍有其他问题）

• **实际任务优先派**：坚持只有用户真正关心的任务才是有效评估标准，游戏这类基准的唯一方法就是真正变得更好（xnx）。实际使用体验、成本和完成任务的正确性远比benchmark分数重要（throwatdem12311以DeepSeek为例说明性价比的重要性）

• **基准怀疑派**：认为基准测试本身存在系统性问题——模型可以在测试中表现优异但实际使用体验糟糕（cryptolobster）。一旦某物成为基准就不再是好基准（functionmouse），类似Firefox放弃主流浏览器基准的先例

• **演化论者**：承认基准测试问题很多但仍然必要，需要不断演化的基准生态系统来应对作弊，尽管存在6.9%误差率等问题（astro1234）

补充讨论：有评论批评文章本身充斥AI生成痕迹（StilesCrisis），cyanydeez开玩笑说最好的基准是不告诉任何人的基准，Legend2440从相关性vs因果性角度解释Goodhart定律的根源。

data.title: When online commenters detect my art as AI
data.author: Jare
data.article_summary:
艺术家David Revoy分享了一组来自Reddit、YouTube、Instagram、Facebook等平台的评论截图，展示了大量网友指责或质疑他的手绘作品是AI生成的。尽管他分享了创作延时视频证明作品的真实性，但这类评论仍在增加且态度愈发强硬。

作者拥有20多年的在线艺术作品，这些作品未经授权被用于AI图像生成模型的训练数据。如今在2026年，他反而成为AI"检测"的目标，面临真实性质疑的困境。这种经历启发他创作了第64期每周漫画《真实性问题》，希望让读者理解当代艺术家面临的这一悖论处境：原创作品反被误认为AI生成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：知名艺术家David Revoy的手绘作品被网友误认为AI生成，引发关于AI对创意产业影响的讨论。

不同观点：

• **明显是人工创作派**：指出作品细节经得起推敲（如爱丽丝插画中扑克牌、火烈鸟等细节清晰合理），且艺术家有大量AI时代前的作品集、Krita教程和开源文件可证明。批评指责者连基本的Google搜索都不做就妄下结论。

• **理解误判派**：承认作品风格确实像AI生成，但这可能恰恰因为AI模型是用这类流行的奇幻/科幻艺术风格训练的。认为这位艺术家的作品处于"中间地带"——是各种流行艺术风格的融合，而这正是AI模型平均化的结果。

• **创意贬值担忧派**：认为AI泛滥导致人们本能地不相信作品背后有真实投入，创意工作被严重贬值。强调AI"发现"容易但真正"创造"困难，因为艺术价值无法预先设定标准（如梵高生前无人欣赏的例子）。

• **开源困境派**：借此反思更广泛的开源问题——创作者公开作品后反被指控抄袭，而他人却用其代码牟利。这种经历让许多人对开源失去热情。

补充讨论：有评论者赞赏艺术家公开完整的Krita源文件，认为这是真正的开源精神；也有人指出这类"被指控PS/AI"的现象早在生成式AI之前就存在，只是AI让问题更普遍了。核心争议在于AI时代如何保护和认可人类创作者的价值。

• **明显是人工创作派**：指出作品细节经得起推敲（如爱丽丝插画中扑克牌、火烈鸟等细节清晰合理），且艺术家有大量AI时代前的作品集、Krita教程和开源文件可证明。批评指责者连基本的Google搜索都不做就妄下结论。

• **理解误判派**：承认作品风格确实像AI生成，但这可能恰恰因为AI模型是用这类流行的奇幻/科幻艺术风格训练的。认为这位艺术家的作品处于"中间地带"——是各种流行艺术风格的融合，而这正是AI模型平均化的结果。

• **创意贬值担忧派**：认为AI泛滥导致人们本能地不相信作品背后有真实投入，创意工作被严重贬值。强调AI"发现"容易但真正"创造"困难，因为艺术价值无法预先设定标准（如梵高生前无人欣赏的例子）。

• **开源困境派**：借此反思更广泛的开源问题——创作者公开作品后反被指控抄袭，而他人却用其代码牟利。这种经历让许多人对开源失去热情。

补充讨论：有评论者赞赏艺术家公开完整的Krita源文件，认为这是真正的开源精神；也有人指出这类"被指控PS/AI"的现象早在生成式AI之前就存在，只是AI让问题更普遍了。核心争议在于AI时代如何保护和认可人类创作者的价值。

data.author: shuklaayush
data.article_summary: 本文探讨如何优化RISC-V虚拟机的执行性能，使其接近裸机运行速度。作者在开发OpenVM（一个生成执行证明的RISC-V虚拟机）时发现，解释器模式下程序运行速度比原生慢30-40倍。文章分析了传统解释器的性能瓶颈：在fetch-decode-execute循环中，解释器在指令管理（取指、解码、分发）上花费的时间往往超过实际执行时间。为突破这一限制，作者提出使用提前重编译（AOT recompiler）技术，通过尾调用连接生成的基本块，并利用Clang的preserve_none调用约定将热点客户机状态保持在主机寄存器中，从而显著减少虚拟机开销，提升执行效率。

• **架构层面解决方案**：MiroslavPokorny提出操作系统应支持LLVM式中间表示，在加载时生成本地代码，从根本上消除对模拟器的需求，解决跨CPU架构兼容问题

Pushing the limits of RISC-V emulation
2026-07-26
Cop

Contents
TL;DR
This post explores how close a RISC-V program can get to bare-metal performance on a non-RISC-V machine. The key is an ahead-of-time recompiler that connects generated basic blocks with tail calls and uses Clang’s
preserve_none
calling convention to keep hot guest state in host registers.
Lately, I’ve been working on
OpenVM
, a RISC-V virtual machine we’re building at
Axiom
. It runs a program and, along with the output, produces a
succinct cryptographic proof
1
that the execution was correct. During my time at Axiom, proof generation has scaled from a single CPU to
clusters of GPUs
by distributing the workload across multiple nodes. However, the first step remains unchanged: we still have to run the program and record its execution. The proving phase is embarrassingly parallel and scales well with additional hardware, whereas execution is inherently sequential. As proving continues to scale, execution speed increasingly becomes the bottleneck, and this post is about making that step faster.
When I started looking into execution, I kept coming back to a simple question:
how fast should a program run?
OpenVM runs RISC-V programs compiled from normal languages like Rust, so I could compile the same program natively for my machine and use that as a baseline. On an M3 MacBook, the native arm64 program finished in about 100 milliseconds, while the same program took three or four seconds through our interpreter. I expected the virtual machine to be slower, since running through it necessarily adds overhead, but not by orders of magnitude.
The fastest way to run a program is to get out of its way and let the hardware execute it directly. A virtual machine cannot simply hand the program to the hardware because it has to maintain control over the execution and bridge the gap between the guest
2
and the host. Instead, it either interprets the program or translates it into instructions the host can understand. The rest of this post explores how far we can push this idea, starting with a basic interpreter and progressively removing the layers of overhead between the guest and the host.
The interpreter baseline
A straightforward way to run RISC-V
3
code is with an interpreter that loops through the classic fetch-decode-execute cycle.

arm64 assembly

uint32_t
word
=
fetch
(memory
,
pc)
;
Instruction inst
=
decode
(word)
;

+=
4
;
switch
(inst
.
opcode) {
// dispatch + execute
case
OP_ADDI
:
write_reg
(inst.rd
,
regs[inst
.
rs1]
+
inst.imm)
;
break
;
case
OP_ADD
:
write_reg
(inst.rd
,
regs[inst
.
rs1]
+
regs[inst
.
rs2])
;
break
;
// ...
}
}
L_dispatch

ldr     w9, [x20, x19]             // fetch the guest
word
add
x19, x19, #
4
// advance the guest pc
bl
decode                     // decode its fields
ldr     x10, [x21, x0,
lsl
#
3
]     // select the opcode handler
br      x10                        // dispatch
h_add
:
ldr     x9, [x22, #t0_offset]
ldr     x10, [x22, #t1_offset]
add
x11, x9, x10
str
x11, [x22, #t2_offset]
b       L_dispatch                 // return to the
loop
The problem is that guest instructions are often tiny. An add or a shift may only perform a single arithmetic operation, while the interpreter has to fetch the instruction, decode its fields, select the right case in the
switch
, and maintain its own execution state along the way. The interpreter can end up spending more time managing instructions than executing them.

Example: a decoded RISC-V instruction
An R-type instruction, such as
add rd, rs1, rs2
, uses a fixed layout for its fields:
+--------------+----------+----------+--------+----------+--------------+
|    funct7    |   rs2    |   rs1    | funct3 |    rd    |    opcode    |
+--------------+----------+----------+--------+----------+--------------+
|    31:25     |  24:20   |  19:15   | 14:12  |   11:7   |     6:0      |
+--------------+----------+----------+--------+----------+--------------+
The
opcode
identifies the instruction’s encoding class. The
funct3
and
funct7
fields further narrow this down to the specific operation within that class, while
rd
,
rs1
, and
rs2
identify the registers involved.
For example,
add x5, x6, x7
, which computes
x5 = x6 + x7
, fills in these fields as follows:
+--------------+----------+----------+--------+----------+--------------+
|    funct7    |   rs2    |   rs1    | funct3 |    rd    |    opcode    |
+--------------+----------+----------+--------+----------+--------------+
|    0000000   |  00111   |  00110   |  000   |  00101   |    0110011   |
+--------------+----------+----------+--------+----------+--------------+
Here
rd
,
rs1
, and
rs2
refer to registers
x5
,
x6
, and
x7
respectively. The
opcode
,
funct3
, and
funct7
fields together select the
add
operation.
A
sub
instruction uses the same
opcode
and
funct3

funct7
from
0000000
to
0100000
.

49182946.article_content:
Companion code on GitHub
Notebooks & source for this series —
DataForScience/LLMs
→
That Basic Harness loop is correct, but
naive
. A lone pilot in a well-built jet might win a dogfight, but nobody runs an air campaign that way.
Real operations
add mission planners who decide what sorties to fly before anyone takes off, squadrons that fly independent sorties in parallel, fuel budgets and bingo calls that force a return to base before the tanks run dry, flight recorders that make every mission reconstructible after the fact, and after-action reviews that decide whether the mission actually succeeded. None of these replace the pilot. They wrap the pilot in structure so that the whole system stays fast, safe, debuggable, and measurable.
Claude Code, Devin, Cursor, Hermes, and other production agents do exactly the same thing to the basic loop. In this post we upgrade every piece of our basic harness toward that production shape, without hiding any of the mechanics behind a framework. The guiding question for the whole exercise is a simple one:
How do you turn a single LLM call into a reliable system that can plan, act, recover, and prove it did the right thing?
Our answer is composition. We build small, testable primitives: typed tools, a plan
DAG
, tiered memory, a verification hierarchy, budgets, and a tracer, and wire them together with a deliberately thin orchestrator. Each primitive exists because naive agents fail in a specific, predictable way. LLMs invent invalid tool arguments, so we add typed tools with
Pydantic
validation. Everything runs sequentially, so we add a dependency graph and parallel execution. The context window fills with junk, so we add multi-tier memory under a retrieval budget. Bad outputs propagate silently, so we add a verification hierarchy. One prompt tries to do everything, so we split it into
Planner
,
Worker
, and
Critic
roles. Costs run away, so we add multi-dimensional budgeting with graceful degradation.
Proving the harness
usually
works, with an eval suite, retrieval benchmarks, and specialized worker pools will get a full fledge treatment in a future post.
The running example
Throughout the post we build a city comparison agent: given a list of cities, it produces a report comparing them on population, timezone, and a short narrative summary of each. The task looks almost insultingly simple, but it was chosen carefully. Each city-attribute lookup is independent of every other one, which means a three-city request naturally decomposes into nine tool calls that could all run at the same time. The final report, on the other hand, depends on all of the lookups finishing first, so we’re. well beyond a flat list of steps. We can programmatically check that every requested city actually appears in the report to verify the results. And the tools have wildly different costs: population and timezone lookups are in-memory dictionary reads, while the per-city summaries and the final aggregation each call the LLM, which gives us realistic budget pressure to manage.
For the sake of reproducibility, lookup tools read from a small mocked dictionary,
CITY_FACTS
, so the notebook is fully reproducible without network access. The LLM-backed pieces can run against either a real Anthropic model or a deterministic mock, which brings us to the first primitive.
A pluggable brain
Every component we are about to build eventually calls an LLM: the planner, the summarizer, the aggregator, the critic. If that call is hard-wired to one SDK, the entire harness becomes untestable and vendor-locked.
So before anything else, we define a base class that provides an abstraction over the details of the various LLM calling APIs

LLMProvider
:
"""Shared interface. Subclass to plug in a different backend."""

complete

str

We also implement a
MockProvider
for testing and debugging purposes that returns deterministic, role-aware responses: a canonical plan when asked to plan, a templated one-line summary when asked to summarize, a rule-based pass/fail verdict when asked to judge. This allows us to separate “is my orchestration wrong?” from “is the model planning badly?” during development, and it is the reason every experiment in this post is reproducible on any machine.
Typed tools
In the
basic harness
we validated tool arguments by hand, an approach collapses quickly: every new tool duplicates validation logic, the LLM never sees a formal schema and just guesses argument shapes, and the resulting errors are ad hoc strings the model can’t self-correct from.
The upgrade is to declare each tool’s arguments as a Pydantic model and let one definition drive everything:

data.title: Online Friends Are Real Friends
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary:
作者通过自身经历探讨了网络友谊的真实性。他即将第六次与六年前在Reddit上认识的好友见面，这段经历让他反思：网络朋友可以和现实朋友一样真实，甚至更真诚。

作者指出，网络交流让人更容易敞开心扉，分享私密想法。与现实中可能出于便利而建立的友谊不同，网络友谊更多基于纯粹的兴趣和个性契合。他的网络朋友遍布美国、德国、荷兰、奥地利、阿塞拜疆和俄罗斯等国，他们定期联系、互相关心、交流生活目标，甚至寄送礼物。

作者强调，遇到紧急情况时，他首先想到的往往是这些网络朋友。无论是网络还是现实中的朋友，只要建立了真诚的连接，都是"真正的"朋友。

主要讨论点：在线友谊是否具有与线下友谊同等的真实性和价值

不同观点：

• **支持派**：在线友谊同样真实且有优势。kator通过游戏认识妻子并结婚20年，认为没有外貌和简历的干扰，反而能更快了解一个人的真实性格、处事方式和价值观。nazgulsenpai的最好朋友都来自网游，强调在线友谊对忙碌者更有意义

• **质疑派**：在线友谊缺乏现实约束力。en3r0和PeterStuer认为在线关系可以随时放弃，缺少真实友谊需要经历的冲突和对抗。mihaic最为激进，将其比作"在线性爱"，强调人类进化需要物理存在才能建立真正的社交联结

• **中间派**：友谊的核心在于投入程度而非媒介。brailsafe认为真正的友谊来自"尽管不便仍相互投入"，在线或线下只是形式区别。win311fwg质疑"在线朋友"分类的必要性，现代人都通过电子设备联系

补充讨论：MomsAVoxell提醒有些人只适合文字交流，见面反而失望；0xDEAFBEAD担心AI技术使在线交友面临诈骗风险；tomwheeler提出判断标准——真朋友关心你人生结局

Re: Online Friends Are Real Friends
29 Jul, 2026
A few days ago I booked my flights to not only attend a professional event, but also visit and stay with one of my best friends next month. This will be the sixth time that at least one of us has traveled to hang out with the other.
We met each other online six years ago via Reddit (and to some degree, Instagram back when I still had an account) simply through shared interests. Never in my life did I suspect I would befriend someone online to such a degree that they feel like a true brother to me.
I liked
Absurd Pirate's post
because it made me reflect on my own online friendships, which are so important to me.
First of all, I don't consider just anyone who talks to me as my friend. There's a solid difference between acquaintances and friends, and there are other platonic dynamics that exist somewhere in between those two labels. I certainly have both online and in-person contacts with whom I look forward to interacting on occasion either via phone call or at a café to catch up. And while I don't doubt that these folks care about me and vice-versa, I don't feel any sense of urgency to communicate with them (and again, probably vice-versa). It's okay if we don't really chat outside of those one or two times per year, and I tend to not seek help or guidance from them. They're something more than acquaintances, but at the same time not quite friends.
As Absurd Pirate notes, online friends have quickly become the norm. Still, I've noticed that it's still kind of strange to some that many of the people to whom I'd reach out first if I found myself in an emergency or a sticky situation are just that—online friends. And not online friends in the sense that one of us moved away from each other, but rather that we met somehow via the Internet, and the potential of us interacting in person would otherwise be more or less zero if not for the digital world introducing us and growing that desire to hang out in real life.
I without a doubt agree that online friends can be just as "real" as those who are physically near you. I've shared some and listened to pretty personal shit with online friends. And maybe that's why my online friendships can often be "realer" than my IRL ones. Like many, I find it easier to be vulnerable when I'm behind a screen. I think that relatively greater openness as well as the number of niche communities on the Internet help open more opportunities to kindle such genuine friendships.
In addition, there's generally a lower chance that the friendship develops out of convenience alone. Don't get me wrong, many in-person friendships are born this way and can turn into the most meaningful lifelong connections. And most people looking for real friendships generally aren't so shallow. But when I'm chatting with someone online who lives far away and they know I have no favors to offer them physically or financially (not to say this is impossible via virtual relationships, but you get what I mean), then I feel more secure in that they want to get to know me purely for who I am or at least spend time together via a hobby that can be practiced virtually.
My online friends and I know who each other's in-person friends are. We help each other navigate tricky professional or social situations. We check in on each other when we're going through tough times. We make sure to call or at least message each other regularly, and we begin to worry when we don't hear from the other person for a couple weeks. We share art with each other. We exchange foreign languages to better connect and help each other improve at a hobby important to us. We send each other notes and small gifts in the mail. We discuss our goals and aspirations in life.
I don't even do all those things with some of my IRL friends.
My online friends are spread across countries: the United States, Germany, the Netherlands, Austria, Azerbaijan, and Russia. I've actually been lucky enough to meet most of my online friends in person, even if only once. These are some of my favorite memories, and I'm always waiting for the day we can finally hang out in person again.
I think each of my friends knows me in a different way, whether they are online or IRL. But some friends definitely know me better than others, and those tend to be my online ones.
It's not that I struggle so much to befriend others in person. However, as someone who often feels a disconnect between herself and the immediate world around her, I value very much what my online friends bring into my life, be it an interest I cannot reasonably pursue in my current city or an entirely different but refreshing outlook on the world.
That being said, I'd love to host all my online and IRL friends together at a dinner party someday. Because they're all my "real" friends no matter what.

Aristotle, one of the most influential philosophers of ancient Greece, laid foundational ideas in ethics, logic, politics, and natural sciences that continue to shape our understanding of the world today. A student of Plato and tutor to Alexander the Great, Aristotle established his own school, the Lyceum, where he explored diverse topics, from biology to metaphysics. His work continues to be a source of timeless wisdom, especially in the realms of virtue, knowledge, and happiness.
In this post, we’ve compiled 25 of Aristotle’s most profound quotes, each accompanied by insights to help understand his teachings. These quotes, primarily from his works

and
Metaphysics
, reveal his approach to living a fulfilled and virtuous life.
1. “We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.”
This statement emphasises the role of habits in shaping character, suggesting that consistent virtuous actions lead to excellence, making it a part of one’s nature. Delve into Aristotle’s exploration of ethics in
Nicomachean Ethics
, where he elaborates on virtues, moral character, and the pursuit of a flourishing life.
2. “Happiness depends upon ourselves.”
Aristotle believed happiness (eudaimonia) is achieved through a life of virtuous actions and self-improvement, emphasising personal responsibility in attaining happiness. Learn more about Aristotle’s view of happiness as a life-long pursuit in
Nicomachean Ethics
.
3. “Educating the mind without educating the heart is no education at all.”
For Aristotle, true education nurtures both intellectual and moral virtues, shaping not just one’s intellect but character. Aristotle explores this balance in
Politics
and
Nicomachean Ethics
.
4. “Knowing yourself is the beginning of all wisdom.”
Self-awareness is central to Aristotle’s philosophy, as understanding one’s character is the foundation for moral development. He addresses self-knowledge as a vital aspect of the good life in
Nicomachean Ethics
.
5. “He who has overcome his fears will truly be free.”
Aristotle saw courage as essential to virtue, arguing that facing fears leads to freedom from emotional constraints. Explore his views on courage as a moral virtue in
Nicomachean Ethics
.
6. “Friendship is a single soul dwelling in two bodies.”
Aristotle regarded friendship as one of the highest goods, rooted in mutual respect and shared virtues. For his complete discourse on friendship, see
Nicomachean Ethics
, Book VIII.
9. “Good habits formed at youth make all the difference.”
Aristotle emphasised the importance of early moral education, believing virtues developed in youth lead to lifelong character. This is a recurring theme in
Nicomachean Ethics
.
7. “The aim of the wise is not to secure pleasure, but to avoid pain.”
True wisdom, Aristotle believed, involves seeking a life free from unnecessary pain rather than pursuing fleeting pleasures. His thoughts on pleasure and virtue are developed in
Nicomachean Ethics
.
8. “Pleasure in the job puts perfection in the work.”
Aristotle believed that engaging wholeheartedly in work leads to fulfillment and excellence. He explores the link between satisfaction and productivity in
Nicomachean Ethics
.
10. “It is the mark of an educated mind to be able to entertain a thought without accepting it.”
This quote reflects Aristotle’s belief in critical thinking, where considering diverse viewpoints fosters wisdom. See more in
Metaphysics
, where he explores open-mindedness in intellectual inquiry.
11. “Happiness is the meaning and the purpose of life, the whole aim and end of human existence.”
Aristotle identified happiness as the ultimate goal of human life, achieved through virtuous living and fulfillment of one’s potential. He elaborates on this idea in
Nicomachean Ethics
.
12. “In all things of nature, there is something of the marvelous.”
Aristotle’s appreciation for nature reflects his curiosity about the world and his belief in the interconnectedness of all life.
Physics
offers a deeper dive into his views on natural wonders.
13. “The energy of the mind is the essence of life.”
This quote underscores Aristotle’s view that intellectual vitality is central to a purposeful life. Learn more in
Metaphysics
, where he discusses the nature of the mind and spirit.
14. “A friend to all is a friend to none.”
Aristotle argued that true friendships require selectivity and genuine mutual appreciation.
Nicomachean Ethics
contains a full discussion of Aristotle’s views on different types of friendship.

data.article_summary:
法国将从8月11日起实施新法律,全面禁止未经消费者事先同意的电话营销。这项由马克龙政府支持的法律采用强制性"选择加入"机制,企业必须获得消费者明确授权才能拨打营销电话。

该法律旨在应对长期以来的消费者投诉——约四分之三的法国人每周至少接到一次骚扰电话。违规者将面临严厉处罚:个人最高罚款75,000欧元,企业最高罚款375,000欧元。

这项禁令对摩洛哥呼叫中心产业造成冲击,可能影响多达5万个工作岗位。德国、荷兰等国也已实施类似禁令,而美国、加拿大和英国则采用"拒绝来电"登记系统。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• **支持禁令且认为有效**：澳大利亚通过严格执法（百万美元级罚款）和要求明确选择加入的机制，成功遏制了合法营销电话，仅剩非法诈骗电话

• **强调执法重要性**：单纯立法不够，需要建立有效的举报和处罚机制，能够在国家层面封禁或罚款骚扰号码

• **指出执行困难**：西班牙案例显示营销商转用国际号码绕过禁令；许多电话来自监管薄弱的第三世界国家，执法困难

• **质疑禁令合理性**：企业持续进行电话营销是因为确实有效，质疑是否有更好的客户接触替代方案

PARIS (AP) — France next week will ban unsolicited telemarketing calls under a new law aimed at protecting consumers from intrusive sales pitches and shielding vulnerable people from fraudulent commercial practices.
The law backed by President Emmanuel Macron’s government enters into force on Aug. 11.
While several countries have tried opt-out systems, France is hoping more muscular obligatory opt-in rules will be more effective.
Here’s a look at the law and its potential impact.
People have been complaining for years
Previously in France, people who wanted to avoid marketing calls had to register their number with a government-run service, but consumer groups said some call centers ignored the list.
Now, “businesses are prohibited from contacting consumers without their prior consent,” said Alice Vilcot, chief of staff at the Directorate-General for Competition, Consumer Affairs and Prevention of Fraud. “That consent can be withdrawn at any time.”
The government says the law is a response to years of consumer complaints. Authorities estimate that about three-quarters of people in France receive at least one unsolicited sales call every week, and many receive more.
In 2024, 11 consumer organizations issued a joint call for a ban, denouncing “relentless harassment of consumers through countless unwanted telemarketing calls to both landlines and mobile phones — an intrusion that has become a regular part of their daily lives.”
Parliament approved the law last year.

1 MIN READ
An unwanted call faces fines of up to 375,000 euros
Individuals who make illegal calls can be fined up to 75,000 euros ($87,000) per call. Companies can face fines of up to 375,000 euros ($435,000) per call.
There are exceptions. Consumers may consent to receive marketing calls, for example by checking a consent box on a form. Companies can contact customers with new commercial offers if they already have a contractual relationship.
Read More
People can report unsolicited calls through a government website.
Vilcot noted that an Ireland-based company was fined 6 million euros ($6.9 million) last year for violating France’s previous telemarketing rules by calling people on the no-call list.
Morocco raised concerns over job impact
France’s new law has raised concerns in Morocco, where the minister of employment, Younes Sekkouri, told lawmakers up 50,000 jobs were at risk in the country’s call centers. Sekkouri said the industry has attracted around $100 million in investment and generates more than $1 billion in annual revenue in the country.

Low labor costs, a large French-speaking workforce and relatively weak unions have made Morocco an attractive outsourcing destination for international companies, particularly French firms seeking to reduce costs.
Youssef Chraïbi, president of the Moroccan Federation for Outsourcing Services, told the local daily Le Matin that the French market has historically accounted for more than 80% of the industry’s revenue.
“Pure telemarketing now represents only 15% to 20% of total activity,” Chraïbi said, adding that the sector has increasingly diversified beyond traditional call center services.
Other countries have tried to limit calls
Neighboring Germany has had a similar ban since 2009.
The Netherlands tightened rules on telemarketing calls last month. The country had already banned unsolicited sales calls but now, companies are not allowed anymore to call their own customers with promotional offers without previous authorization.
Many other countries rely on opt-out systems.

data.title: Why Erdős Problems Are Falling to AI
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary:
这篇文章报道了AI在数学领域的重大突破。2026年5月，OpenAI宣布其AI模型找到了传奇数学家Paul Erdős在1946年提出的"单位距离"问题的反例，这是首个由AI完成的历史性数学证明。8月，OpenAI又宣布其Astra模型解决了另外3个Erdős问题。

Erdős是20世纪最多产的数学家之一，一生提出数千个数学问题并悬赏求解。他生活简朴，四处旅行，依靠安非他明维持高强度的数学研究。英国数学家Thomas Bloom在2023年创建了erdosproblems.com网站来收集整理这些问题。

数学界认为这些进展标志着AI数学能力的"相变"，正在深刻改变数学研究的方式。Erdős问题因其简洁性和深度成为AI能力的重要试金石。

主要讨论点：AI在数学领域取得突破后，人类数学家的角色、AI能力的本质以及这一进展的真实意义

不同观点：

• **忧虑派**（throwatdem12311）：担心专业数学家都无法理解AI的突破，质疑如何辨别真伪，担忧人类智力被超级计算机替代

• **乐观转型派**（delhanty）：认为AI擅长找反例，数学家应转型为"理论解释者"，专注于向人类阐释AI成果，而非单纯追求新定理

• **技术派**（pfdietz）：认为AI具有广泛数学知识储备和耐心，未来可自动生成猜想并验证，强调自动形式化的重要性

• **质疑派**（operation_moose, vatsachak, m3kw9）：质疑AI是否真正创新，认为可能只是连接已有知识、模式识别或组合现有论文

• **阴谋论派**（12k5ha）：认为报道是Renaissance Fund的隐性广告，质疑报道的客观性

• **未来展望派**（bsaul）：强调当数学突破扩展到物理、化学、生物领域时，将产生更深远的实际影响

补充讨论：争议焦点在于AI数学突破的"深度"——是真正的创造性突破还是高效的知识整合？以及人类在AI时代的智力角色定位问题。

Why the Legendary Erdős Problems Are Falling to AI
By
Konstantin Kakaes
August 3, 2026
AI’s greatest mathematical successes have come from answers to problems posed by a mid-20th century iconoclast. By examining what makes the Erdős problems unique, mathematicians are trying to understand how AI might change the rest of math.

O
n May 20, 2026, OpenAI made an announcement that shook the mathematical world. An internal AI model — one not available to the public — had come up with a
counterexample to the “unit distance” problem
, a conjecture made in 1946 by Paul Erdős, the prolific, itinerant Hungarian mathematician.
Erdős posed thousands of questions, but this one was special: It was both simple to explain and mathematically deep. It was the first historically significant proof to come from an AI model. Though the model’s result wasn’t definitive — human mathematicians would substantially improve on it within weeks — it was innovative, bringing in ideas from a distant branch of math that no one had successfully applied to this problem before. And it was influential: Within a few days, related techniques were used to solve other important problems.
Then on August 1, OpenAI
announced
that an unreleased model named Astra made 10 additional mathematical advances, including finding solutions to three more problems posed by Erdős.
Many mathematicians have hailed developments such as these as a phase transition in the mathematical capability of AI models. These models are “changing dramatically the way mathematical research is being done,” said
Noga Alon
of Princeton University, who has solved dozens of Erdős problems over his decades-long career.
Paul Erdős, one of the most prolific mathematicians in history, was deeply whimsical when it came to mathematics, and deeply cynical when it came to authority.
Photo by George Csicsery from the documentary
N is a Number: A Portrait of Paul Erdős
©1993. All Rights Reserved.
Erdős and his conjectures have long fascinated mathematicians. He traveled constantly — living out of a suitcase for years at a time, staying with friends, owning almost nothing. He rattled off problems in published papers and letters to mathematicians around the world, often attaching prize money that he would pay out of pocket to the first person to come up with a solution. The reward might be a token $10 or $25, or, for problems he considered important or difficult, it could range into the thousands. Erdős died of a heart attack in 1996 while attending a math conference in Warsaw, but a nonprofit foundation based in Iowa
has promised
to make good on his bounties.
He was a beloved figure, but also a downright weird one. He only wore silk, and he avoided the touch of other people. Deeply cynical about authority, he gave away most of the money he earned and relied on a friend to manage his finances and other practical affairs. He referred to God as the “Supreme Fascist” and fueled his incessant output of mathematical ideas with a steady diet of amphetamines. It is a strange irony of history that the problems he suggested have now become a central proving ground — and, in effect, a series of PR coups — for the world’s biggest and most powerful technology companies.
But in all likelihood none of this would have happened had it not been for an English mathematician named
Thomas Bloom
.
Many Meetings
Like Erdős, Bloom was interested in both number theory and combinatorics. His focus has been an area called arithmetic combinatorics, which lies at the intersection of the two. After getting his doctorate in 2014, Bloom established himself as a rising star in the field, landing a
prestigious fellowship from Britain’s Royal Society
, which let him work at almost any university he wanted to. (He’s now at the University of Manchester.)
Bloom has liked Erdős’ style for as long as he can remember. But he always found it hard to keep track of which problems had been solved and which had been forgotten entirely. So in early 2023, he decided to gather as many problems as he could into a list.
He intended it for his own use. But “I thought it would be easier if I could access it wherever I was,” he said; he figured he “might as well make a website, kind of with the expectation that maybe nobody would use it.” He gathered a couple hundred problems and launched

data.title: Show HN: Wallfacer – A terminal session manager for Claude Code, and more
data.author: pradiptasarma
data.article_summary:
wallfacer 是一个终端会话管理工具，专为 Claude Code、Cursor CLI、Kiro CLI 和 Codex 等AI编码助手设计。

**核心问题**：这些AI工具会在本地生成大量未命名的会话文件，分散在不同目录中，难以管理和查找。

**解决方案**：wallfacer 通过只读方式索引所有会话文件，将元数据存储在本地SQLite数据库中，提供统一的管理界面。

**主要功能**：
- 统一查看所有agent的会话记录
- 为会话命名、添加标签、分组到项目
- 跨标题、目录、标签搜索
- 启动新会话或恢复历史会话
- 安全删除（先移到回收站）
- 提供全屏TUI浏览器和CLI命令行两种操作方式

**安装**：支持Homebrew或Go安装，需要Go 1.22+版本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Claude Code 会话管理工具 Wallfacer 的必要性、命名争议，以及 2026 年开源工具的价值定位

不同观点：

• **支持派**：feintruled 和作者 pradiptasarma 强调实际需求 — 在大型项目中，Claude Code 会话按目录存储为 JSON，难以追踪和恢复之前的对话。现有的 /resume 功能因目录绑定而不够用，需要专门的搜索和管理工具。

• **替代方案派**：sunir 认为可以用 /rename 命名会话配合 tmux 解决问题；tim-projects 质疑为何要重新发明 tmux；d4rkp4ttern 分享了自己基于 Rust/Tantivy 的类似工具方案。

• **哲学质疑派**：pelasaco 提出深层思考 — 既然现在可以用 AI 快速编写定制工具，为什么还要使用别人开发的通用工具？这反映了 2026 年开源生态的变化。

• **命名争议**：laszlojamf 对"Wallfacer"（面壁者）这个《三体》系列概念表示不安，担心代理会秘密策划对抗用户。

补充讨论：Arshad-Talpur 怀旧式地回忆 GitHub 开源搜索的黄金时代，鼓励继续构建。整体讨论反映出工具类开源项目在 AI 编程时代面临的身份认同问题：当每个人都能快速生成定制工具时，通用开源工具的价值边界在哪里？
